title: Education The Monthly Dispatch -- What's New in Learning Science? -- June 2026 Hendrick, Carl
author: Hendrick, Carl
summary: Carl Hendrick's June 2026 Monthly Dispatch synthesizes recent learning science research across four areas: new boundary conditions on retrieval practice, a further failure to replicate generic thinking skills transfer, a finding on cognitive tool dependency, and the retraction of the most-cited meta-analysis supporting AI in learning. New research shows retrieval practice stops working when cognitive load from material complexity is too high. A study on generic thinking skills training again found no transfer to related domains, reinforcing the domain-specificity of expertise. Research on removing cognitive tools found that students who relied on a tool showed greater performance declines when it was removed than students who never used it. Most significantly, the Wang and Fan meta-analysis that has been the primary citation for claims that AI improves learning has been retracted by Nature.
points: Retrieval practice fails when cognitive load from material complexity exceeds working memory capacity -- the additional processing demand of active retrieval cancels the benefit, a boundary condition practitioners teaching genuinely demanding content must account for.

Generic thinking skills training -- teaching 'how to think' as a transferable skill independent of domain knowledge -- again failed to produce transfer to related tasks, reinforcing decades of evidence that expertise is domain-specific.

Research on cognitive tool dependency found that removal of a tool harmed performance more than the tool's presence helped it -- with direct implications for calculator use, AI writing assistance, and any instructional scaffolding intended to be eventually removed.

The retraction by Nature of the Wang and Fan meta-analysis -- the most-cited paper supporting claims that AI improves learning -- removes the primary scientific foundation for a large body of edu-tech marketing and should prompt reassessment of AI adoption decisions made on that basis.

The science of learning is a probabilistic enterprise: each new boundary condition or retraction does not invalidate prior findings but narrows the conditions under which those findings reliably apply -- a nuance most popular accounts of learning research omit.
quotes: New research on retrieval practice shows it stalls under high cognitive load. Generic thinking skills again fail to transfer to related tasks. Removing a cognitive tool, it turns out, hurts more than adding it ever helped.
context: New research shows retrieval practice stops working when cognitive load from material complexity is too high.
